metadata.goal: Analyze the recurring mobility patterns associated with frequent call-center callers, considering possible aspects.
metadata.header: Recurring Mobility of Frequent Porto Taxi Callers
metadata.dataset_description: A constructed set of exactly 500 call-center taxi trips from eight pseudonymous frequent callers. Every caller has at least two caller-specific dominant pickup areas, while the three callers with shifting pickup focus have three, four, and six dominant areas. Road-aligned GPS traces and caller profiles support dominant-area recurrence, within-year shifts, within-caller dominant-area linkages, and departure-time analysis.

insight_list.insight: Frequent callers typically request taxis from at least two recurring dominant pickup areas, while callers whose pickup focus shifts across the observation year use three to six dominant areas.

insights: Frequent callers typically request taxis from at least two recurring dominant pickup areas, while callers whose pickup focus shifts across the observation year use three to six dominant areas.
Trips originating in one of a caller's dominant pickup areas usually end in another dominant area belonging to the same caller.
A large share of trips are concentrated between morning and noon, especially for trips originating from the callers' dominant pickup areas.
summary: All eight callers rely on multiple recurring dominant pickup areas. Five callers retain a stable primary focus across the year, while three shift their focus within larger sets of three to six dominant areas. Trips beginning in one caller-dominant area usually end in another dominant area belonging to the same caller, and dominant-area departures are particularly concentrated between morning and noon.
